subject: home air filter
title: What If You Never Changed Your Air Filter?

scenes.text: What if you never changed your air filter? Your home keeps breathing, through a dirtier and dirtier mask.
The US Department of Energy says to clean or replace it every month or two in cooling season.
After a few months it clogs. Less air squeezes through, and the system has to work harder to cool.
Then air sneaks around the filter, dumping dirt straight onto the cooling coil and insulating it.
A clean filter can cut air conditioner energy use by 5 to 15 percent. A clogged one throws that away.
Energy Star warns a dirty filter can damage the equipment and cause early failure. A cheap filter, an expensive mistake.

description:
What if you never changed your air filter? The US Department of Energy says a clogged filter cuts airflow, lets dirt bypass onto the evaporator coil, and that replacing it can lower air conditioner energy use by 5 to 15 percent.
Energy Star warns a dirty filter can also damage the equipment and lead to early failure.
